contracts.protected_resource: The project settings. file at Path.cwd()/.{app_name}/settings., together with the SECRET_FIELDS and IDENTITY_FIELDS exclusions.
contracts.protection_obligation: Default settings persistence must split by trust: the project ./.{app_name}/settings. receives only PROJECT_SETTABLE_KEYS fields; every other user-scoped key goes to the user config, and SECRET_FIELDS/IDENTITY_FIELDS are never written, so the repo-visible project file cannot accumulate keys the loader would refuse or leak secrets.
scope_limits: An explicit path= argument switches to a legacy single-file full dump of all non-secret, non-identity keys, bypassing the allowlist split (settings_persistence.py:187-191).

Keys the save does not manage (hand-stored secrets, unknown domain keys) are preserved verbatim in the user file by merge-write; a malformed user file raises rather than being clobbered (settings_persistence.py:202-216).
Secrets (SECRET_FIELDS) and identity fields (IDENTITY_FIELDS) are excluded from every write (settings_persistence.py:22-29, 63-66, 179-182).

scope_limits: Filters only the project ./.{app_name}/settings. and a cwd-relative .env; environment variables (AGENTIC_*), constructor kwargs, the user-level ~/.{app_name}/settings., and absolute/user-level env_file entries remain fully trusted (config.py:274-336; settings_persistence.py:31-43).

When any configured env_file entry is cwd-relative the whole dotenv source is filtered (over-filtering fails safe); per-file filtering is not possible (config.py:310-319).
